clue.text: What makes crust start to rise in pie?

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed inside the word for the pie

parts.note: a pasty is a ... case with a filling, a kind of pie

indicators.note: the start of the word rise gives only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A baking question: what makes a pie's crust begin to rise in the oven?
explanation.walkthrough: A PASTY is a Cornish filled pastry, a British handheld pie. Put R, the start of 'rise', in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is the dough that is baked to form the crust of a pie or tart.

clue.text: Buy tea bag on the way round

indicators.note: the purse wraps round the slang word for tea

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Picking up tea and a bag while out and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way' is padding for the surface; cha is old British slang for tea, as in 'a cup of cha'.
explanation.definitionFit: To purchase is to acquire by paying, a straight synonym for buy.

clue.text: Prue's new chap is one with great abilities

indicators.note: new letters are a fresh arrangement of the name and its s

parts.note: the name Prue with its possessive s, five letters of fodder
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Prue's new boyfriend is remarkably talented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns PRUES into SUPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero has superhuman powers, so he is someone of exceptional abilities.

clue.text: Check of presents?

parts.note: presents here are people who answer 'present' when their names are read out, not gifts

explanation.surface: Someone checking the pile of gifts at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading names aloud to see who answers 'present' is a check on attendance, so it checks the people present.

clue.text: English journalists will tuck in exceedingly and drink

indicators.note: the journalists tuck themselves inside the word for exceedingly

parts.note: so, as in 'so kind', means exceedingly
the press is the collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: English reporters tucking into a meal and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck in' suggests eating, but here it means the journalists go inside the word for exceedingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong black coffee, a kind of drink.

clue.text: After short time, speed becomes uninspiring

indicators.note: the speed word comes after the short time

parts.note: a second is a brief moment
rate means speed, as in rate of travel

explanation.surface: A runner's pace slows after a brief burst, and the race turns dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre and inferior in quality is described as not first class, hence dull and uninspiring.

clue.text: Cause long-term irritation in right joint

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: A chronic ache in the right leg joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to continue to cause bitterness or resentment over a long time.

clue.text: Teacher misses motorway pressure

indicators.note: the teacher misses out the motorway's letters

parts.note: a mistress is a female schoolteacher
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A teacher stuck in traffic who misses the motorway, under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: MI stands for the M1, the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or tension applied, a synonym for pressure.

clue.text: Old boy is to broadcast as orchestra member

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of is and to are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil is going on the radio as part of an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio but scatters IS and TO into OIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, a woodwind instrument in the orchestra.

clue.text: Place found in rickety pier causing undulation

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place is found inside the rearranged letters
something rickety is shaky and falling apart, so the letters of pier are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PL is the usual abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Something odd is discovered in a shaky seaside pier, making it sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' rearranges the pier into RIPE before the abbreviation goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripple is a small wave or undulation on a surface.

clue.text: One car is overturned in plan of action

indicators.note: the words one, car and is are upset and their letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describing an accident: one car has flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' looks like a reversal but is the anagram signal for ONECARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a sketched-out sequence of events, a possible course of action.

clue.text: Poet's house next to watercourse

definitions.note: the definition is the poet; the 's stands for 'is'

parts.note: a race is a channel of water, as in a mill race

explanation.surface: A poet's home stands beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintus Horatius Flaccus was a Roman lyric poet of the age of Augustus.

clue.text: Alan's suffering little sister following day's end breakdown

indicators.note: the short sister comes after the day's last letter
suffering suggests being in a bad way, so the letters of Alan are rearranged

parts.note: the name Alan, its possessive adding no letter

indicators.note: the end of the word day is its final letter

parts.note: sis is a short, familiar form of sister

explanation.surface: Alan and his kid sister both struggling at the end of a day, close to a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' turns ALAN into ANAL; 'day's end' gives Y. Breakdown here is an analysis, not a collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown of figures is a detailed examination of them, which is what an analysis is.

clue.text: Award one fails to win

parts.note: a joke prize goes to the person who finishes last, so failing earns it

explanation.surface: An award that someone fails to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'fails to win' as 'wins by failing': the prize goes to the loser.
explanation.definitionFit: A consolation prize given in jest to whoever comes last in a contest.

clue.text: Little time for sleep?

parts.note: the hours just after midnight have low numbers, little hours, and are the time most people sleep

explanation.surface: A complaint about not getting enough rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Little time' as hours with small numbers (one, two, three in the morning), not as a shortage of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The early hours after midnight, when most people are asleep, carry this idiomatic name.

clue.text: Pump provided by men in apartment above

indicators.note: in a down answer the flat sits above the men

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A pump supplied by workmen in the flat upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword's usual 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflator is a device that fills tyres or balls with air, a pump.

clue.text: Urged United to support 27 opponents

indicators.note: in a down answer the united word sits below the opponents, holding them up

parts.note: 27 across is a card game whose players are East and North, among others, and E and N sit on opposing sides
joined means united

explanation.surface: A football team urged to back the rival players.
explanation.walkthrough: At the bridge table North-South play East-West, so East (E) and North (N) are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoin someone is to direct or urge them to do something.

clue.text: Eat with wife — have outside in warm spell

indicators.note: the word have goes round the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dining al fresco with your wife in hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A heatwave is a period of unusually hot weather.

clue.text: Not drinking as sailors can — leading French in this?

indicators.note: the can comes ahead of the French words

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors
a tin is a can
en is the French word for in
ce is the French word for this

explanation.surface: Teetotal like sailors who drink from cans, with the French setting the example?
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' applies to both 'in' and 'this', giving EN and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining from something, especially alcohol, so it is a state of not drinking.

clue.text: Verify said money order

indicators.note: the word for verify is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to check something is to verify it

explanation.surface: An instruction to confirm a payment instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEQUE is the British spelling of the bank document.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order to a bank to pay a sum of money.

clue.text: Help musician starting late

indicators.note: starting late means the musician's word loses its first letter

parts.note: a bassist plays the bass guitar or double bass

explanation.surface: A band asks for help because a player has turned up late.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Declared Scots know to get half of spoils beforehand

indicators.note: the half of spoils comes before the Scottish word
the first half of the word spoils, three of its six letters

parts.note: ken is Scots for know

explanation.surface: Scots announcing that they know who takes half the loot first.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken words are uttered aloud, so a statement made orally has been declared.

clue.text: Squirts rush out when it's played on the lawn

definitions.text: Squirts rush out when it's played on the lawn

parts.words: Squirts rush out when it's played on the lawn
parts.note: a garden water tube is played over the grass, like a jet aimed at a fire, and water squirts out

explanation.surface: Children rushing outside when a lawn game starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' suggests a game or a tune, but here it means directing a jet of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible tube used to water a garden sends out squirts of water when directed on the grass.

clue.text: 'Nearly all.' — 'Nearly all?' — 'Nearly …'

indicators.note: nearly all of the word all means it stops one letter short

parts.note: most is a word for nearly all

explanation.surface: A conversation that keeps trailing off, each speaker saying less.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Nearly all' works on the word itself, giving AL; the second is a synonym, MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost is a plain synonym for nearly, as in very close to.

clue.text: Living with cook as a temporary solution

parts.note: quick means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'
to fix a meal is to cook it

explanation.surface: Living with someone who cooks as a stopgap arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: QUICK for living is the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty stopgap remedy that does not address the root problem is a stock phrase for a short-term fix.

clue.text: Ollie's partner's spoken a few lines

indicators.note: the possessive name is said out loud, giving a word of verse

parts.note: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner was Stan Laurel, so this gives Stan's

explanation.surface: Laurel and Hardy talk: Ollie's partner speaks a few lines of dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Ollie and Stan are the comic double act Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Old and sore — stretcher required?

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
a tender spot is sore to the touch

explanation.surface: An old, aching patient who might need carrying on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The stretcher here lengthens things rather than carrying the injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes an item longer stretches it, so a lengthening device is a stretcher.

clue.text: Game groom's first to be hugged by future relative

indicators.note: the groom's letter is held inside the word for the future relative

parts.note: a bride is about to become a relative by marriage

indicators.note: the first letter of the word groom

explanation.surface: At a wedding, the groom is hugged by his future in-law.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDE hugs G, the first of 'groom's'. The game is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships.
